Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.

mcqs.q: Why does plastic accumulate in ocean gyres?
options: Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.

Gyres are large rotating ocean currents driven by wind and Coriolis effect; floating debris is carried in but the rotation traps it in the centre, where currents are weak, concentrating plastic over decades.
The 'Great Pacific Garbage Patch' is a solid floating island of plastic you can walk on.
Plastic accumulates in gyres because the water there is denser.
